feedback.problem: A particle $P$ is moving along the curve $y=2{x}^{2}-3{e}^{x}$ such that the $x$-coordinate of $P$ is changing at the rate of $2\,\text{cm}/\text{s}.$ Find the rate of change of the $y$-coordinate when $x=2\,\text{cm}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =2{x}^{2}-3{e}^{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{x}^{2}-3{e}^{x}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{2}-3{e}^{x}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (4x-3{e}^{x}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=2\,\text{cm}/\text{s}$ and $x=2$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =2(4\cdot (2)-3{e}^{2})\,\text{cm}/\text{s} \\  & =2(8-3{e}^{2})\,\text{cm}/\text{s}.\end{aligned}
$$
